text:
Happy Friday! The cold front has mostly moved through, and any leftover sprinkle this morning is a few hundredths of an inch at most. We stay mostly cloudy early, then get some sun this afternoon with a high near 54, cooler than yesterday. A few outlets run warmer, but I'd stay in the 50s with that cloud. It's breezy at times, and with dry leaves everywhere it's a day to be careful with anything that sparks. Tonight clears out and drops to around 34, so bring the jacket.

Halloween is the better half of the weekend. Saturday is sunny and calm, with a high near 50, though some guidance sits in the upper 40s. Trick-or-treat hours should be clear, but temperatures slide through the 40s toward the 30s, so plan an extra layer under the costume. Saturday night falls to around 30, so expect frost on the windshield Sunday morning. Remember to set the clocks back an hour before bed.

Sunday brings more sunshine and a milder afternoon, with a high near 57. It's a good day for a long walk or ride, and the extra hour of morning light helps. Sunday night stays mild, around 41.

Looking ahead, Monday turns cloudier and warmer. A weak front may bring a spotty shower late Monday into Tuesday, but most of us should stay dry.

AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: The cold front continues to move through the region this morning, with dwindling rain showers and plentiful cloud cover along with it. Rainfall amounts with this feature have generally been a few hundredths, although some locations across northern New York have observed a few tenths on an inch of rain. Strong cold air advection will take place behind the front today, with increased clouds and some chances for some lingering showers in the favored upslope areas with some flurries possible in the higher terrain. Temperatures on Friday will be more seasonable compared to yesterday, with highs in the upper 40s and 50s. Heading into the weekend and the start of next week, surface high pressure looks to build into the region once again. This will lead to another stretch of dry weather, with ample sunshine, light winds, and pleasant conditions to round out October and welcome the start of November. Temperatures on Saturday will be a little on the cooler side, with highs generally in the mid 40s to low 50s, moderating towards the start of next week. KEY MESSAGE 2: Breezy winds and lower relative humidity values will lead to increased fire weather concerns over the next few days, especially given the plentiful dry leaf litter across the area serving as fuel. Wind gusts today and Friday will generally be in the 15 to 25 mph range, with some higher gusts are possible. Minimum relative humidity values will generally be between 40 to 55 percent for today. Heading into the weekend, minimum relative humidity values should drop into the 30 to 45 percent range, but winds look to be much lighter. Recent rainfall amounts remain rather negligible, with most locations only receiving a few hundredths of an inch, but a few locations across northern New York received over 0.1 inches of rain with these showers. Cloud cover across the region today will help limit some of these fire weather concerns. KEY MESSAGE 3: There remains little change to the details regarding a frontal boundary expected to shift southwards Monday night into Tuesday. Upper level vorticity will shift east, and an incoming ridge will help dissipate the front. It's very possible it does not even make it to the international border, but a handful of scenarios depict it reaching at least far northern Vermont. For late Tuesday into Wednesday, a surface low will lift from the Plains north towards James Bay. It will send a warm front into the region. Better moisture and dynamics will remain well to our north and west as surface high pressure moving from far eastern Canada into the maritimes will keep stable, southeasterly flow filtering into the region. Again, some rain could develop with a handful of forecast scenarios depicting light rain along the international border. Thereafter, the large scale pattern amplifies.
